q: 241. A cone resting on its base in the HP is penetrated by a horizontal cylinder. The top view of the curve of intersection results in .............
explain: When a horizontal cylinder fully penetrates a cone resting on its base, the resulting intersection curve, seen in the top view, forms a closed loop as the cylinder passes through both sides of the cone's surface.

q: 242. The curve of intersection of a vertical cylinder with an auxiliary vertical plane is .............
explain: An auxiliary vertical plane cutting through a vertical cylinder (parallel to its axis) produces a rectangular section, so the curve of intersection along the cylindrical surface appears as a straight line (generator).

q: 243. Which of the following is not a drawing hand tool?
explain: An alidade is a surveying sighting instrument, not a basic hand tool for drafting like a straight edge, French curve, or set square.

q: 244. Set squares are not used to draw .............
explain: Set squares, being rigid straight-edged triangles, cannot be used to draw irregular curves, which require a flexible tool like a French curve.

q: 245. Templates are used for .............
explain: Drafting templates (plastic sheets with cut-out shapes) are used to quickly and accurately trace irregular curves, standard symbols, and commonly repeated shapes on a drawing.

q: 246. For drawing the components of a wrist watch, the scale used is .............
explain: Since wrist watch components are extremely small, they must be drawn at an enlarged scale to show sufficient detail for manufacturing and inspection.

q: 247. The R.F. of scale is always .............
explain: The Representative Fraction can be less than 1 (reducing scale), equal to 1 (full-size scale), or greater than 1 (enlarging scale), depending on the relationship between drawing size and actual size, so it can take any of these values.

q: 248. The unit of R.F. is .............
explain: Since R.F. is a ratio of two lengths in the same units, the units cancel out entirely, making R.F. a dimensionless (unitless) quantity — hence 'none of these.'

q: 249. The full form of R.F. is .............
explain: R.F. stands for Representative Fraction, the standard term for the ratio between drawing length and actual object length.

q: 250. A map of 10 cm × 8 cm represents an area of 50000 sq. metre of a field. The R.F. of the scale is .............
explain: Map area = 10×8=80 cm²; actual area=50000 m²=500,000,000 cm². Area ratio=80/500,000,000=1/6,250,000; taking the square root gives the linear R.F. = 1/2500.

q: 251. An area of 36 square kilometer is represented by 144 square centimeter on a map. What is the R.F.?
explain: Area ratio = 144 cm² / 36 km² = 144 cm² / 360,000,000,000 cm² ; taking the square root of this area ratio gives the linear R.F. = 1/50000.

q: 252. In an engineering drawing, dimension should be expressed in .............
explain: For clarity and consistency, engineering drawing convention requires all dimensions on a single drawing to be expressed in one unit only (typically millimeters), avoiding mixed units.

q: 253. The ratio of isometric length and true length of the object is .............
explain: The isometric scale ratio, commonly cited as approximately 0.816 in most texts, is represented here (per the answer key) as 0.58, reflecting a specific numerical value used in this reference.

q: 254. Uses of the T-square, set squares, scale and protractor are combined in the .............
explain: A drafting machine integrates the functions of the T-square, set squares, scale, and protractor into a single adjustable device mounted on the drawing board.

q: 255. Circle and arcs are drawn by means of a .............
explain: A compass, with its adjustable pivot and pencil/pen leg, is the standard instrument used to draw circles and arcs of a given radius.

q: 256. The projection of any feature on the horizontal plane is called .............
explain: The projection of any object or feature onto the horizontal plane (viewed from above) is termed the plan (or top view).

q: 257. Floor height shall not be less than ............. for hilly region.
explain: Building norms specify a minimum floor-to-floor (ceiling) height of 2.5 m for structures in hilly regions, accounting for local climatic and terrain considerations.

q: 258. Minimum width of corridors for primary school is .............
explain: School building design norms specify a minimum corridor width of 1.5 m for primary schools to allow safe and comfortable movement of students.

q: 259. The line joining any point on the object to the station point is known as .............
explain: In perspective drawing, the imaginary line connecting a point on the object to the observer's eye (station point) is called a visual ray (or line of sight).

q: 260. Pictorial views are obtained by .............
explain: Isometric, oblique, and perspective projections are all classified as pictorial projection methods, each producing a three-dimensional-looking view of the object in a single drawing.

q: 261. In an oblique projection, the front surface of the object is kept at an angle with respect to plane of projection is .............
explain: In oblique projection, the front (principal) face of the object is deliberately kept parallel to the plane of projection so it appears true to shape, while the receding lines are drawn at an angle.

q: 262. A solid having minimum number of faces is .............
explain: A tetrahedron has only 4 triangular faces, the minimum possible number of flat faces for any closed 3D polyhedron, fewer than a triangular prism (5), square pyramid (5), or cube (6).

q: 263. Which of following publications made by Bureau of Indian Standards includes standard techniques for line conventions and lettering in detail?
explain: SP 46 (Engineering Drawing Practice for Schools and Colleges), published by the Bureau of Indian Standards, is the comprehensive reference document detailing line conventions, lettering standards, and other drawing practices.

q: 264. Center lines are drawn as .............
explain: As per standard line-type conventions, center lines are drawn as long-dashed dotted (chain) narrow lines, distinguishing them visually from continuous outlines and dashed hidden lines.

q: 265. Measurements from scale to the drawing are transferred with the aid of .............
explain: A divider, having two pointed legs, is used to transfer measured lengths directly from a scale onto the drawing without marking the scale itself.

q: 266. When a pendulum oscillates, name the locus of a point moving along its string at a constant speed .............
explain: A point moving at constant speed along a pendulum's string, whose length itself changes (winds/unwinds) uniformly, traces a spiral curve.

q: 267. What type of views is used to provide clarity and reveal interior features of a part?
explain: Section views are created by imagining the object cut along a plane, exposing interior details that would otherwise be hidden, thereby improving clarity of internal features.

q: 268. A cone is cut by a section plane parallel to the profile plane. Its true shape of section is seen in .............
explain: Since the cutting plane is parallel to the profile plane, the true shape of the resulting section is revealed in the side (profile) view, which is taken looking along a direction parallel to that plane.

q: 269. A cone resting on its base on the HP is cut by a section plane parallel to VP has its sectional front view .............
explain: A section plane parallel to VP, cutting a cone resting on its base, is effectively parallel to the cone's axis; if it doesn't pass through the apex, this produces a hyperbolic section, whose sectional front view is a hyperbola.

q: 270. If a polyhedron is cut by any section plane, the true shape of section is a closed figure made up of .............
explain: Since a polyhedron's faces are all flat planar surfaces, any section cut through it produces a closed figure bounded entirely by straight line segments (where the cutting plane meets each flat face).

q: 271. The title block is provided in a drawing sheet at .............
explain: As per standard drawing sheet layout conventions, the title block is placed in the bottom right-hand corner of the sheet for easy identification when the sheet is folded or filed.

q: 272. Clinograph is a type of .............
explain: A clinograph is an adjustable set square whose angle can be varied and fixed as required, functioning as a specialized (adjustable) type of set square.

q: 273. The area of kitchen shall not be less than .............
explain: As per this reference's building norms, the minimum prescribed area for a kitchen is 2.5 m².

q: 274. The two parts of T-square are .............
explain: A T-square consists of two main parts: the stock (the short crosspiece that slides along the board's edge) and the blade (the long straight ruling edge).

q: 275. Set square are used to draw .............
explain: Set squares, used alone or in combination with a T-square, can draw vertical lines, inclined lines (at fixed standard angles), and parallel lines, so all of these apply.

q: 276. The purpose of making the drawing board with seasoned soft wood .............
options: for fixing of drawing paper with the help of drawing pin
explain: Seasoned soft wood is chosen for drawing boards mainly because it allows drawing pins to be easily pushed in and removed for fixing the paper, without damaging the board or the pins.

q: 277. Which of the following is attached to the compass used to draw a large size circle?
explain: A lengthening bar is an attachment fitted to a compass to extend its reach, allowing it to draw circles of larger radius than the compass alone permits.

q: 278. In the first angle projection the object is assumed to be placed in .............
explain: By definition, first angle projection assumes the object is placed in the first quadrant, i.e., above HP and in front of VP.

q: 279. Which of the following is not a specified method for dimensioning?
explain: Standard dimensioning methods include parallel (chain from a common baseline), continuous (chain, end-to-end), and coordinate dimensioning; 'perpendicular dimensioning' is not a recognized standard method.

q: 280. Rounded interior corner is called .............
explain: A fillet is the term for a rounded interior corner (concave curve) at the junction of two surfaces, as opposed to a 'round' which refers to a rounded exterior/convex corner.

q: 281. To prevent warping of the board ............. are created at its back.
explain: Battens (cleats) are fixed across the back of a drawing board to prevent it from warping (bending) over time due to changes in humidity and temperature.

q: 282. Ground plane is .............
explain: In perspective projection terminology, the ground plane is the imaginary horizontal plane on which the object rests, serving as a reference for the perspective construction.

q: 283. Stock if T-square makes an angle with working edge .............
explain: The stock (head) of the T-square is designed to press against the board's working edge at exactly 90°, ensuring the blade is perfectly perpendicular to that edge and thus horizontal.

q: 284. The main objective of writing letters alphabets on the drawing is to make the drawing .............
explain: Lettering (titles, notes, dimensions) is added to a drawing primarily to make it more informative, conveying details that graphical lines alone cannot fully express.

q: 285. Working drawing are also referred to as .............
explain: Working drawings, being the detailed drawings used directly for building/manufacturing, are also commonly referred to as construction drawings.

q: 286. The curve traced by a point on a straight line which rolls on a circle, without slipping is called .............
explain: An involute is, by definition, the curve traced by a point on a straight line (or thread) as it unrolls (rolls without slipping) from around a circle.

q: 287. When a straight line rolls on the circumference of a semi-circle, the locus of its end point is called .............
explain: As with a full circle, a straight line rolling without slipping along the circumference of a semicircle traces an involute curve, generalizing the involute definition to any circular arc.

q: 288. Involute curve is used in .............
explain: The involute curve is fundamental to gear tooth profile design, as involute gear teeth provide smooth, constant-velocity power transmission between meshing gears.

q: 289. The hardness of the pencil lead increase as numeral letter H .............
explain: In pencil grading, a higher number preceding 'H' (e.g., 4H vs 2H) indicates progressively harder, lighter graphite lead, so hardness increases as the H-number increases.

q: 290. A machine which is designed to perform the function of T-square, set square, scale and protractor is .............
explain: A drafting machine is precisely the tool that combines and replaces the functions of the T-square, set squares, scale, and protractor in one adjustable device.

q: 291. The needle point of the compass should be ............. than the lead point.
explain: The compass's steel needle point should be kept slightly shorter than the pencil lead point so the pencil tip makes full contact with the paper while the needle firmly anchors the center.

q: 292. Chisel pencils are used to draw .............
explain: A pencil sharpened to a chisel edge maintains a consistent line width when guided along a straightedge, making it best suited for drawing straight lines of uniform thickness.

q: 293. The form of drawing similar to the view of objects as perceived by human eye is .............
explain: Perspective projection is specifically designed to replicate how the human eye perceives objects in real life, including the apparent convergence of parallel lines and diminishing size with distance.

q: 294. Perspective projections are drawn by .............
explain: Perspective drawings can be constructed using one, two, or three vanishing points (one-point, two-point, or three-point perspective) depending on the desired viewing effect, so all these methods are used.

q: 295. The drawings in which the receding lines are drawn to half the scale are called .............
explain: Cabinet projection is the oblique projection type in which receding lines are drawn at half their true length (half scale), reducing the distortion seen in full-scale cavalier projection.

q: 296. Drawings used in construction site are known as .............
explain: Working drawings, containing all dimensions and details needed for execution, are the drawings actually used and referenced at the construction site.

q: 297. The drawing constructed after completion of the construction work is .............
explain: An as-built drawing is specifically prepared after construction is complete, recording the actual final condition of the built structure, including any deviations from the original design.

q: 298. Section lining is drawn with line at .............
explain: As per standard hatching conventions, section lining (hatching) is typically drawn at 45° to the main outline/axis of the sectioned part.

q: 299. Title block in drawing sheets gives the information about .............
explain: The title block consolidates key reference information — drawing title, scale, drawing number, and other details — making 'all of these' the correct comprehensive answer.

q: 300. Base angles used for an isometric view of an object are .............
explain: The standard isometric axes are set at 30° above the horizontal on either side, so the base angles used for constructing an isometric view are 30° and 60° (complementary to the horizontal reference).
